code_fixes_in_this_reissue.source: KNOWN_ISSUES.md BEN-023; AUDIT-FINDINGS-20260731.md J10 (tier B) and J35 (tier A).
what_was_wrong: train_fullevent_nominal.py wrote the publication nominal with a bare np.savez_compressed straight to --out: no temp file, no os.replace, no no-clobber guard. An interrupted train (preemption, walltime, node failure) therefore left a nonempty, plausible, INCOMPLETE npz at the publication path.
That partial was then indistinguishable from a result: every `[[ -s $OUT ]]` resume guard in the tree reads it as finished, and the Gate-4 validator would have read it as a nominal to certify.
numpy appends '.npz' to a name that lacks it, so the driver's success line could name a path that does not exist.
what_changed: The write goes through atomic_write.atomic_savez_compressed: a temp sibling in the destination directory, fsync, then os.replace -- so --out is either the previous file or the whole new one, never a partial. The temp is removed on any failure.
mark=True stamps a completion marker LAST, so a marker always implies a fully published artifact and never the reverse. lib/resume_guard.sh reads the same marker format.

A no-clobber guard runs BEFORE training: an output that already carries a VALID completion marker is not silently replaced (--allow-overwrite opts in). A partial leftover carries no marker and is freely overwritten, which is the case the old behaviour got backwards.
The driver reports the path actually written, not the path requested.
code_fixes_in_this_reissue.not_changed: No physics. Same arrays, same keys, same seeds, same fold-forward sums, same reporting spectra, same cap-saturation fraction. Gate-4's validator reads an identical npz.
